item.title: NID rollout underway in Moresby South
item.description: A civil registration and national identification [NID] rollout program is underway across the Moresby South electorate to ensure residents have access to basic state identity services. The program, which commenced on September 21, focuses on issuing NID cards and birth certificates for children under 20 years of age, covering eligible records registered between 2015 and 2020.
item.content:encoded:
A civil registration and national identification [NID] rollout program is underway across the Moresby South electorate to ensure residents have access to basic state identity services.

The program, which commenced on September 21, focuses on issuing NID cards and birth certificates for children under 20 years of age, covering eligible records registered between 2015 and 2020.

Supported by Moresby South MP Justin Tkatchenko, the project is being facilitated through the Moresby South District Administration under district administrator Aisop Mol, in partnership with the PNG Civil and Identity Registry .

Described as an effort to bring government services closer to the people, the rollout operates across designated collection points spanning from 6-Mile through to Kone .

Collection points established across the electorate include Sabama Police Post, Koki Transit Market House, 6-Mile Saraga Market, and Gereka Police Post .

Tkatchenko urged residents who have registered or are eligible for documentation to visit the designated sites to collect their identity documents .

item.title: Daulo MP passes on
item.description: Member for Daulo, Ekime Mek Gorosahu passed on at Paradise Private Hospital in Port Moresby today. United Resources Party leader William Duma confirmed the death of his party colleague, describing the news as devastating.
item.content:encoded:
Member for Daulo, Ekime Mek Gorosahu passed on at Paradise Private Hospital in Port Moresby today.

United Resources Party leader William Duma confirmed the death of his party colleague, describing the news as devastating.

“It is true. Heartbreaking,” Duma told NBC News.

Details surrounding the cause of death have not yet been released by official sources or family representatives.

Gorosahu’s death brings the total number of MPs who have died during the 11th National Parliament to nine.

A first-term Member of Parliament, the late Gorosahu served on the Permanent Parliamentary Committee on Culture and Tourism.

item.title: PNG targets 2028 exit from grey list
item.description: Papua New Guinea is expected to exit the global grey list by 2028, according to the body tasked with managing the country’s compliance response. The National Coordinating Committee [NCC] on Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing [AML/CTF] confirmed that a comprehensive three-year strategy is underway to address requirements set by the Financial Action Task Force [FATF].
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea is expected to exit the global grey list by 2028, according to the body tasked with managing the country’s compliance response.

The National Coordinating Committee [NCC] on Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing [AML/CTF] confirmed that a comprehensive three-year strategy is underway to address requirements set by the Financial Action Task Force [FATF].

Financial Analysis and Supervision Unit [FASU] director Wilson Onea said the action plan spans 2026 to 2028 and outlines realistic targets for technical and operational compliance.

“The action plan is a three-year action plan which includes 2026, 2027, and 2028,” Onea said.

“It is practical and doable. Based on experience, a country that exits quickly usually takes between 18 months and three years.

“Taking a conservative view, we are targeting 2028.”

Onea was speaking at the 2nd Anti-Money Laundering, Counter-Terrorism Financing, and Counter-Proliferation Financing Conference in Port Moresby.

NCC chairman Dr Eric Kwa likened the country’s multi-layered reform program to a game of strategy, emphasizing that work is taking place across all technical thresholds simultaneously.

“I tell the team about the game Jenga (Sushi Game),” Kwa said.

“You remove the blocks carefully so the structure doesn't collapse.

“The 17 immediate action conditions are at the top, but we also have 42 underlying requirements that we monitor every quarter.

“While we address the top priorities, we are systematically working through the foundational areas as well. We are confident we can achieve this.”

item.title: K150m ready for election prep: PM
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape has confirmed that K150 million budgeted for 2027 national election preparations is ready for release, with an additional K50 million set aside for security operations. Speaking at Jackson’s International Airport on Tuesday after returning from the United Nations General Assembly in New York, Marape urged the Electoral Commission to exercise strict financial discipline
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape has confirmed that K150 million budgeted for 2027 national election preparations is ready for release, with an additional K50 million set aside for security operations.

Speaking at Jackson’s International Airport on Tuesday after returning from the United Nations General Assembly in New York, Marape urged the Electoral Commission to exercise strict financial discipline and avoid unnecessary spending.

He said the allocated funds must go directly towards primary logistical priorities, including the procurement of ballot boxes, updating the common roll, and rolling out security preparations.

“Don’t waste the K150 million we are going to pass through,” Marape said.

“Procure the ballot papers, procure the ballot boxes, (and) have a clear security plan inside.

“For police and defence, we have about K50 million set aside for police and defence, pre-election planning.

“We want to go into the 2027 elections prepared well so you people can cast a ballot and vote on a leader of your choice that you feel can best represent you.

“So I want to also indicate we are planning well for Election 2027, and Electoral Commissioner, very soon your commission will receive K150 million.”

Marape’s assurance on election funding comes on the heels of an internal audit undertaken by the Electoral Commission, which led to the suspension of several senior officers.

Former acting electoral commissioner Margaret Vagi and deputy commissioner Kila Vane are among those suspended.

item.title: Over 120 graduate from UOG’s IDFL program in Madang
item.description: More than 120 students are graduating today from the University of Goroka’s Institute of Distance and Flexible Learning [IDFL] in Madang. Graduands will be conferred with Bachelor degrees in school management - a program tailored for in-service teachers seeking professional development, while others will receive diplomas in business management, business administration, tourism and hospitality, and
item.content:encoded:
More than 120 students are graduating today from the University of Goroka’s Institute of Distance and Flexible Learning [IDFL] in Madang.

Graduands will be conferred with Bachelor degrees in school management - a program tailored for in-service teachers seeking professional development, while others will receive diplomas in business management, business administration, tourism and hospitality, and early childhood education.

IDFL executive director Thresa Dingu said this marks the institute's 17th graduation ceremony and the first to be held in Madang under the theme 'Gown to Town'.

"This is the first graduation to be held here for our Madang students, and we are happy to bring the program to them," Dingu said.

"Our Madang students usually travel to the main campus in Goroka for their graduation, but this time we decided to come down to them."

Dingu said Madang IDFL center was established nine years ago and has since graduated more than 1,000 students, with enrollment numbers continuing to grow annually.

UOG acting pro-vice-chancellor Dr Matthew Landu, who is attending the ceremony in Madang, said the university remains committed to expanding distance education pathways.

He thanked the Madang Provincial Government for its partnership following a Memorandum of Agreement signed with UOG in May this year.

Landu added that UOG is actively working to expand flexible learning opportunities to cater to the growing number of school leavers across the country.

item.title: Call for continued leadership as Enga peace project ends
item.description: CARE International PNG has called for sustained leadership and coordination across Enga to safeguard peacebuilding and livelihood recovery efforts as its Wanbel Wantaim [Peace Together] project officially ends today. The call was made during a stakeholder roundtable discussion in Mount Hagen earlier this month, where community leaders and provincial authorities gathered to review the outcomes of t
item.content:encoded:
CARE International PNG has called for sustained leadership and coordination across Enga to safeguard peacebuilding and livelihood recovery efforts as its Wanbel Wantaim [Peace Together] project officially ends today.

The call was made during a stakeholder roundtable discussion in Mount Hagen earlier this month, where community leaders and provincial authorities gathered to review the outcomes of the peace initiative.

Funded by Australia's Minderoo Foundation, the project was implemented across eight communities along the Wabag and Lagaip district corridors, which are areas heavily impacted by tribal conflict, displacement, substance abuse, gender-based violence, and sorcery accusation-related violence.

CARE reported that the project reached more than 4,700 people through the establishment of eight Community Peace Committees, the enforcement of community by-laws, climate-smart agriculture training, and 25 small-grant livelihood projects.

Key infrastructure achievements included the rebuilding of Kaipale Community Primary School and the renovation of three local health facilities.

According to an independent evaluation released by the organization, participating communities showed a noticeable shift toward dialogue and non-violent resolution.

The evaluation highlighted that several individuals voluntarily surrendered firearms, reduced the public carrying of weapons, and stepped away from marijuana, homebrew, and illegal gambling.

It also noted a significant increase in female participation in community leadership and decision-making roles.

Stakeholders from the Enga Provincial Government and project recipients commended CARE’s bottom-up approach, emphasizing that empowering local leadership had driven genuine behavioral change on the ground.

CARE peacebuilding program manager Manu Peter raised concerns about the long-term sustainability of these gains following the project's conclusion.

Peter assured that CARE would continue advocating for broader provincial support to ensure peacebuilding mechanisms remain active across the targeted communities.

Kun Women’s Association representative Merlyn Billy said community unity remains vital.

“Lasting peace requires communities to stand together, respect their by-laws, and support fair justice,” Billy said.

item.title: Six-week land use survey wraps up in Wewak
item.description: A six-week Land Use Survey covering Wewak and Yawasoro townships in East Sepik has concluded, setting the foundation for future township planning and zoning across the province. The exercise was jointly conducted by technical officers from the East Sepik Provincial Administration and the Department of Lands and Physical Planning, supported by the Wewak District Development Authority.
item.content:encoded:
A six-week Land Use Survey covering Wewak and Yawasoro townships in East Sepik has concluded, setting the foundation for future township planning and zoning across the province.

The exercise was jointly conducted by technical officers from the East Sepik Provincial Administration and the Department of Lands and Physical Planning, supported by the Wewak District Development Authority.

Fieldwork commenced in August following stakeholder consultations with the Wewak Urban local-level government [LLG], ward representatives, utility providers, state agencies, businesses, churches, and traditional landowners.

Caretaker provincial administrator Alphonse Ralph Kami said the survey collected vital geo-spatial information on current land use, human settlement, and socio-economic activities to guide future urban growth.

The survey team completed mapping within the gazetted township boundaries of Wewak and Yawasoro before concluding its field operations on Tuesday.

Acting deputy provincial administrator for economic services John Aimos said the exercise is a critical first step towards establishing master zoning plans for both centers.

“Once the Wewak and Yawasoro master zoning plans are launched, we will roll out phases two to eight targeting other district townships such as Angoram, the new Middle Sepik township, Ambunti, Drekikier, Maprik, and Yambi, along with 26 LLG growth centers,” Aimos said.

Information collected during the survey will undergo quality assurance before a draft Land Use Survey Report and zoning maps are submitted to the National Physical Planning Board for endorsement.

Once approved and officially gazetted, the master zoning plans will serve as the statutory framework to regulate future infrastructure and land development.

Kami expressed appreciation to the Department of Lands and Physical Planning, the Wewak District Development Authority, and the East Sepik Provincial Government for their collaboration.

item.title: Local leaders call for BSP mini-branch at Halimbu
item.description: Two prominent community leaders in Hela have called on BSP Financial Group Limited to establish a mini-branch at Halimbu Junction to service the growing economic needs of the Hayapuga local-level government [LLG] area in Tari-Pori district. Community leaders Steven Halimbu and Tobby Maya Pajape made the joint appeal during the official opening of a double classroom at Halimbu Primary School on Sat
item.content:encoded:
Two prominent community leaders in Hela have called on BSP Financial Group Limited to establish a mini-branch at Halimbu Junction to service the growing economic needs of the Hayapuga local-level government [LLG] area in Tari-Pori district.

Community leaders Steven Halimbu and Tobby Maya Pajape made the joint appeal during the official opening of a double classroom at Halimbu Primary School on Saturday, a project funded under BSP’s 50for50 Givim Bek community initiative.

Halimbu said Halimbu Junction, commonly known as Three-Corner, is strategically located as the gateway to the Komo and Hides PNG LNG project sites and the Koroba-Lake Kopiago district, where the Highlands Highway ends.

He said the area is rapidly developing into a vital economic hub for the LLG, with the upcoming commissioning of the new Halimbu Market and plans for a local police station to maintain law and order.

"Given its prime location and growing infrastructure, a mini BSP branch is ideal for Halimbu," Halimbu said.

Pajape supported the call, highlighting that Hayapuga LLG, comprising 21 council wards, is the largest LLG in Tari-Pori, surpassing neighboring Tagali, Tebi, Tari Urban, and Pori LLGs in both land area and population.

Responding to the appeal, BSP Highlands regional area manager John Tomba described the petition as genuine and well-founded.

Tomba said BSP would initially consider establishing BSP agent banking centers in the area to assess customer demand and operational viability before determining the feasibility of setting up a full mini-branch.

item.title: Marape returns from UN General Assembly, warns against taking peace for granted
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape has returned to Papua New Guinea after attending the 81st United Nations General Assembly [UNGA], describing the gathering as successful and productive.

item.title: PNG, Montenegro establish diplomatic relations
item.description: Papua New Guinea and Montenegro have officially established diplomatic ties following the signing of a Joint Statement by Foreign Affairs Minister Justin Tkatchenko and his Montenegrin counterpart Ranko Krivokapic.
